bible_refs.method: wording: 'ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Μεθ' ἡμῶν ὁ Θεός' completes the Isaiah quotation begun in dial-open
bible_refs.note: The gloss on Emmanuel is Matthew's; Isaiah 7:14 is the prophecy behind it.
Listed for the prophecy the gloss explains; cited inline in dial-open.

bible_refs.method: direct quotation: 'παράλαβε τὸ παιδίον καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ φεῦγε εἰς Αἴγυπτον'
bible_refs.note: ἀναστάς for the Gospel's ἐγερθείς; same sense.

bible_refs.method: direct quotation: 'Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ δύναμις Ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι'
bible_refs.note: Ends with 'υἱὸς Ὑψίστου', the wording of Luke 1:32; translated as given.

bible_refs.method: direct quotation: 'ἑαυτὸν ἐκένωσε μορφὴν δούλου λαβών'
wording: 'προέκοπτε σοφίᾳ καὶ ἡλικίᾳ καὶ χάριτι παρὰ Θεῷ καὶ ἀνθρώποις'
bible_refs.note: Woven into Nestorius' own sentence, so not set in quotation marks.

bible_refs.method: direct quotation: 'πᾶν τὸ γενόμενον ἐκ τῆς σαρκὸς σάρξ ἐστι'
bible_refs.note: πᾶν τὸ γενόμενον for the Gospel's τὸ γεγεννημένον; translated as given.

choices.why: Antiochene term (Latin homo dominicus) for the man assumed by the Word; Nestorius uses it as a technical title, so it stays a term.

choices.english: whether you like it or not
choices.why: Plain English for the idiom; keeps Cyril's direct challenge to Nestorius.
rejected: even if you will, even if you will not

choices.why: παράδοξον here is the marvel that passes expectation, not a logical paradox.

choices.english: begets in a manner proper to God
choices.why: τίκτω is used of the Father's begetting of the Son; θεϊκῶς marks the divine manner, set against the Virgin's bearing in the flesh in dial-rem-mid.

pass_a_gloss: [continuing Cyril's quotation of Isaiah 7:14 from dial-open, 'which is'] being interpreted, 'With us is God'. God, therefore, is the one who was born (τεχθείς), whether you will it or you do not will it. [NESTORIUS] The angel said to Joseph: Rising, take along the child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be there until I tell you; but he did not say: Take along God and his mother. [CYRIL] But the archangel Gabriel says to the Virgin: Holy Spirit will come upon you, and power of the Most High will overshadow you; wherefore also the holy thing being born from you will be called son of the Most High. [NESTORIUS] The Apostle said: He emptied himself (ἐκένωσε), having taken the form of a slave; which is: having put on our body, where he was advancing in wisdom and in stature and in grace beside God and men, as a man of the Lord (Κυριακὸς ἄνθρωπος). [CYRIL] All that has come to be from the flesh is flesh; but it does not take away the wonder (παράδοξον) of the birth; for as God brings forth in a divine way (θεϊκῶς), so [the sentence continues in dial-rem-mid]
pass_b_english: …translated, 'God with us' (Matthew 1:23). So the one who was born is God, whether you like it or not.
Nestorius says: The angel said to Joseph, 'Rise, take the child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and stay there until I tell you' (Matthew 2:13). But he did not say, 'Take God and his mother.'

Cyril says: But the archangel Gabriel says to the Virgin, 'The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the holy one who is born of you will be called Son of the Most High' (Luke 1:35).

Nestorius says: The Apostle said, 'He emptied himself, taking the form of a servant' (Philippians 2:7); that is, he put on our body, in which he advanced in wisdom and stature and grace before God and men (Luke 2:52), as the Lord's man.
Cyril says: 'Everything that is born of the flesh is flesh' (John 3:6); yet this does not do away with the wonder of the birth. For just as God begets in a manner proper to God, so…
